 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Gopala Krishna Rao

sentences.text: Judgment:

Aggrieved by the impugned order dated 25.04.2012 on the file of Motor Accident Claims Tribunal -cum- Principal District Judge, Kadapa, passed in M.V.O.P.No.637 of 2009, whereby the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim against the respondents, the instant appeal is preferred by the appellants/ claimants for enhancement of compensation amount.
2.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal -cum- Principal District Judge, Kadapa
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim application.

3. The claimants filed a Claim Petition under section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 read with Rule 475/476 of Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 amended Act No.54 of 1994 against the respondents praying the Tribunal to award an amount of Rs.13,00,000/- towards compensation on account of death of deceased Busam Krishnaiah in a Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 18.05.2009.
2 VGKRJ MACMA 2468 of 2012 4.

Facts germane to dispose of this appeal may be briefly stated as follows:
On 18.05.2009, Busam Krishnaiah, hereinafter referred to as 'deceased', along with his friend M.Pradeep Kumar went to Enagalur on their personal work, after completion of the work, while they were waiting at Enagalur bus stand, the driver of jeep bearing No.AP04U 4920, hereinafter referred to as 'offending vehicle', drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased and ran over him, resulting which, the deceased sustained injuries, later succumbed to injuries.
The petitioners pleaded that the deceased was an employee in Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation, aged about 43 years and claimed an amount of Rs.13,00,000/- towards compensation.

entities.text: Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 5. The first respondent remained exparte.

The second respondent filed counter denying the claim of the claimants and contended that the claimants are not entitled any compensation and the second respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.

sentences.text:
Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
i.

Whether the accident was on account of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the vehicle bearing No.AP04U 4920 and whether the respondents 1 and 2 jointly and severally are liable to answer the claim?
ii.
If so, what is the quantum of compensation that the petitioners 1 to 3 are entitled to and who are liable to pay the compensation?

iii. To what relief?
7.
During the course of enquiry in the claim petition, on behalf of the petitioners, PW1 to PW3 were examined and Ex.A1 to Ex.A5 were marked.
No oral or documentary evidence was adduced on behalf of respondents.

8. At the culmination of the enquiry, after considering the evidence on record and on appreciation of the same, the Tribunal has given a finding that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle, which is insured with second respondent Insurance Company and the Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.5,56,512/- to the claimants towards compensation 4 VGKRJ MACMA 2468 of 2012 from the second respondent.
Aggrieved by the same, the claimants filed the present appeal claiming the remaining balance of compensation amount.

9. Heard Sri D.Kodanda Ramireddy, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri Gudi Srinivasu,
learned counsel for second respondent.
10.

Now, the points for consideration are:
1. Whether the Order of Tribunal needs any interference?
2. Whether the claimants/ appellants are entitled for enhancement of compensation as prayed for?

11. POINT Nos.1 and 2:-
In order to prove the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle,
the petitioners relied on the evidence of PW2.
PW2 is an eye witness to the accident.

The evidence of PW2 goes to show that the deceased and his friend while standing in the extreme left side of the road, taking tea by the side of the tea stall, the jeep came and hit the deceased and left.

The evidence of PW2 coupled with Ex.A1 certified copy of First Information Report and 5 VGKRJ MACMA 2468 of 2012 Ex.A4 certified copy of charge sheet clearly proves that the accident in question was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: As per the evidence of PW3, the Depot Manager of A.P.S.R.T.C., the gross salary of the deceased was Rs.10,132.20 paise per month.
An amount of Rs.100/- has to be deducted towards Professional Tax, then the salary of the deceased is Rs.10,032.20 paise.
The salary of the deceased is taken as Rs.10,000/- per month.
As per Ex.A2 certified copy of Inquest Report and Ex.A3 certified copy of Post Mortem report, the deceased was aged about 43 years.
He was in between 40 and 50 years.
As per the decision of Pranay Sethi's case, 30% of income has to be awarded in addition to the original income towards future prospects.

If 30% of income is added to Rs.10,000/-, it comes to Rs.13,000/-
(10,000 + 3,000) per month.
From out of Rs.13,000/-, 10% of income has to be deducted towards Income Tax, then it comes to Rs.11,700/- (13,000 - 1300) per month.
Since the dependents on the deceased are three in number, 1/3rd of amount has to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
If 1/3rd amount is deducted, an amount of 6 VGKRJ MACMA 2468 of 2012 Rs.7,800/- (11,700 - 3,900) per month was available to the dependents on the deceased, i.e., Rs.93,600/- per annum.
The multiplier applicable to the age group of the deceased is 14.
Accordingly, an amount of Rs.13,10,400/- (93,600 x 14) is awarded to the petitioners towards loss of dependency.
In addition to that, the petitioners are entitled an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards funeral expenses of the deceased and an amount of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of estate.

Accordingly, the appellants/
claimants are entitled an amount of Rs.13,40,400/- towards total compensation. Since the claimants claimed an amount of Rs.13,00,000/- only towards compensation, their claim is restricted to Rs.13,00,000/-.

The Tribunal gave finding in its orders that there are no violations of the policy,
2nd respondent is insurer of 1st respondent and gave finding that both respondents are jointly liable to pay compensation and directed the 2nd respondent Insurance Company to pay the amount.
No appeal is filed by Insurance Company against the said finding.

13. In the result, this appeal is allowed, modifying the order dated 25.04.2012 passed in MVOP No.637/2009 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum- Principal District Judge,
Kadapa, 7 VGKRJ MACMA 2468 of 2012 consequently the claim amount is enhanced from Rs.5,56,512/- to Rs.13,00,000/-.

Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum- Principal District Judge,
Kadapa, 7 VGKRJ MACMA 2468 of 2012
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the appellants/ claimants are entitled the enhanced compensation of Rs.7,43,488/- with interest @6% p.a. from the date of petition, till the date of realization.

The second respondent/Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation amount of Rs.7,43,488/- with interest as ordered above, before the Tribunal within two months from the date of this judgment.

First petitioner is entitled an amount of Rs.2,43,488/-
towards enhanced compensation with interest thereon and the second and third petitioners are entitled an amount of Rs.2,50,000/- each towards enhanced compensation with interest thereon.
The petitioners 2 and 3 are entitled to withdraw their share of enhanced compensation amount after attaining majority.
Until they attain majority, their share of enhanced compensation amount along with accrued interest thereon shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any nationalized bank.
After depositing the enhanced compensation amount, the first claimant is entitled to withdraw her share of enhanced compensation amount along with accrued interest thereon.
There shall be no order as to costs.
8 VGKRJ MACMA 2468 of 2012 Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this appeal shall stand closed.
V.GOPALA KRISHNA RAO, J Dated: 13.09.2023.
